name: Gaia GPS: Offline Trail Maps
price: Free download, core value (offline maps, most layers) gated behind Premium/Outside+ subscription (~$40-90/yr, rising)
complaints: App refuses to open / demands internet login in remote areas, locking users out of paid offline maps exactly when needed
Cannot search maps offline despite offline-map selling point
Post-Outside-acquisition price hikes (~$20/yr jump) and bundling into Outside+ resented by long-time users
Predatory billing: charged $64 for 'free trial', refusal to prorate cancellations, refunds denied
Poor/hostile customer support; reports of accounts terminated after critical reviews
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: AllTrails free tier, CalTopo, Organic Maps/OsmAnd cover casual use, but serious offline topo + layer stacking + track management is under-served free; Gaia's angry base are power users who already pay
moatNotes: No hardware moat. Map-tile licensing (USGS/USFS/OSM) is open; main build cost is layer catalog and offline tile engine. Users explicitly hunting alternatives after Outside acquisition.

name: Sports Tracker: Run Bike Hike
price: Free download; ~3 years ago all key stats (route comparison, progress, workout maps) moved behind Premium subscription
complaints: Formerly-free core stats (compare workouts on same route, progress, maps) paywalled retroactively — classic paywall creep on a 15-year-old install base
Stop button unresponsive for 30+ seconds — workouts can't be ended reliably
Crashes on wearable sync; workouts lost/not saved
Buggy updates: manual-entry dates off by a day, wrong start times
Export features broken even for paying pro users; Suunto/Amer treats it as legacy — Suunto forum users called it 'a complete joke' vs Movescount
freeIncumbentRisk: High-ish: Strava free tier, adidas Running, and phone-native tracking exist — but Strava itself paywalled analytics, which is exactly the displaced-user pool. A one-time-purchase tracker with reliable local stats targets the resentful segment directly.
moatNotes: No hardware moat (works with phone GPS). 16M installs at 3.12 stars is an enormous proven-demand pool. Endomondo/Runtastic refugees already churned here once and got burned again.

name: BackCountry Navigator GPS PRO (TOPO GPS)
price: $11.99 one-time paid (some map sources need extra subscription)
complaints: Developer (CritterMap) shifted all real development to subscription-based successor 'BackCountry Navigator XE'; PRO now gets only Google Play compliance/billing patches
Long-standing bugs unfixed: track recording fails, app crashes when recording
Paid $11.99 owners pushed toward XE membership to stay current — and XE itself rates only 3.44 (470 ratings), so the migration path is also broken
Dated UI/feature set vs modern trail apps
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: OsmAnd, Locus Map (freemium), AlpineQuest Lite serve hobbyists free, but the buyer profile here (hunters, snowmobilers, offline backcountry users per SnoWest forum) demonstrably pays $10+ for offline topo; onX charges $30-100/yr in this exact niche
moatNotes: No hardware moat. Public map sources. The 250k paid installs prove a one-time-purchase offline topo app sells; incumbent abandoned the one-time model, leaving that positioning vacant.

name: 11pets: Pet care
price: Free download; recent rewrite force-migrated users to subscription to access their own existing pet health records
complaints: Update forced subscriptions and blocked long-time users from their previously-entered pet data
Migration lost or scrambled most user data (vaccination records, medical history, photos)
Login broken: users logged out, password-reset emails never arrive
In-app contact/support form literally cannot send messages
New version 'barely functional'; users locked out of countless records and images
freeIncumbentRisk: Low: no dominant free pet-health-record app exists; competitors (PetDesk etc.) are vet-clinic-tethered. Users' #1 need is data safety — local-first storage with export is a direct counter-position to the exact betrayal that tanked this app to 2.1 stars
moatNotes: No hardware moat, no proprietary data. Pure CRUD app (records, reminders, weight charts, multi-pet). The 530k installs prove demand for comprehensive pet care tracking; incumbent destroyed its own trust asset.

name: Zombies, Run! (ZRX)
price: Was $3.99 paid app; since 2015 free-to-play with subscription ($5.99/mo or $39.99/yr) for missions; legacy-buyer perks eroded over successive rebrands (ZRX)
complaints: Original paid buyers migrated to subscription model (2015, v4.0) and perks eroded through later ZRX rebrand — betrayal sentiment among legacy owners
Tracking fails when screen is off (Android battery optimization) — an hour of running logs 30 minutes
Music won't resume after story clips; zombie chases unwinnable even at dead sprint
Subscription demanded mid-way through 8-week training program without warning
Users say devs 'aren't putting in effort' to fix long-standing bugs
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: generic run trackers are free, but story-driven/gamified audio running has essentially no free incumbent — the moat is content. Clone needs narrative audio production (AI-assisted TTS/story generation now makes this cheap).
moatNotes: No hardware moat. Content library is the incumbent's moat, but its tech debt (background tracking broken on modern Android) is the wedge. Rating sits right at the 4.1 threshold — weakest candidate on rating, strongest on category emptiness.
